title: First 10-Minute SDK Runbook — Quick Integration Walkthrough (WIP)
content:
Purpose
This is a minimal, copy-paste friendly runbook intended to get a backend or frontend engineer from zero to the first successful Redwood API call in ~10 minutes. Focus is on the friction points we see in onboarding sessions: API key placement, streaming vs non-streaming, and the most common environment/packaging issues.

Audience
- Engineers who want a very short, deterministic path to success
- Solutions engineers doing live demos / pairing sessions
- Internal DX teammates who need a repeatable checklist for triage

High-level goals
- Success metric: developer can call the SDK and receive a valid response (non-500) within 10 minutes
- Provide copy-paste examples for curl, Node, Python, and a minimal Next.js client example
- Surface 3 common failure modes and quick fixes

Quick checklist (start here)
1) Create API key: Console -> Personal -> API Keys -> Create (note: mark as "demo" if temporary)
2) Install SDK: npm i @redwood/inference or pip install redwood-inference
3) Export key locally: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_demo_xxx (mac/linux) or set via env var in CI
4) Run the minimal example below for your stack
5) If you see 401, verify key scope and expiration in Console; 429 means rate-limited — try a different key or wait

Minimum reproducible examples
- curl (fastest):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \\n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n    -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"Say hi in 3 words"}'

- Node (server-side, minimal):
  // index.js
  import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  async function main(){
    const out = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1-small', input: 'Write a haiku about coffee' });
    console.log(out.text);
  }
  main().catch(e=>console.error(e));

- Python:
  from redwood_inference import Client
  c = Client(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
  resp = c.generate(model='redwood-1-small', input='Two-sentence summary of SRE')
  print(resp['text'])

- Browser / Next.js minimal pattern (recommended: proxy through serverless function):
  Why: API keys must not be embedded in client bundles. For demos, use an ephemeral token via /api/session.

Design notes / rationale
- Keep the server call synchronous for the first run: reduce mental overhead of streaming. After success, add streaming example as an appendix.
- Use small, low-cost model by default (redwood-1-small) so users won’t hit quota surprises.
- Emit clear, actionable error messages in SDK: if 401 -> hint about wrong env var name; if 429 -> include retry-after header in message; if 5xx -> suggest fallback model or offline stub.

Common failure modes and quick fixes
- 401 Unauthorized: most common. Check env var name (REDWOOD_API_KEY vs REDWOOD_KEY), leading/trailing whitespace, and whether key has been revoked. Check Console -> API Keys for scope.
- 429 Rate limit: Demo accounts have tighter limits. Use a different demo key or upgrade the demo account. For local pairing, use token from my "shared demo" key (ask Liam).
- CORS / Client-embed mistakes: Browsers should not call the production API directly. Provide serverless proxy example. If CORS errors occur, verify the dev proxy and ensure Authorization header is forwarded.
- SSL / cert errors in corp networks: If dev sees certificate errors behind corp proxies, suggest setting GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY temporarily for demos or running on a host without the proxy.

Telemetry & observable signals to look for during onboarding
- On SDK startup: emit SDK version and platform (node/python) to our telemetry endpoint (anonymized).
- Track first_success_timestamp for new users — helps identify where friction is concentrated.
- Expose a 'sanity-check' API call (lightweight echo/generate) that returns sample tokens and model info, used by the quickstart UI for live green/red feedback.

Developer experience tips for pairing/demo sessions
- Start with the curl example to show a single round-trip; it demonstrates network/auth working without any SDK issues.
- After curl success, move to Node/Python to show real integration and copy/paste the simple code block.
- Avoid streaming in first demo — streaming introduces websockets/event-source complexities across firewalls.
- Prepare a fallback: a small static JSON response to paste if the API is down during a customer call.

Proposed quick additions to docs (short-term roadmap)
- Add a "first 10 minutes" card to the SDK README with the curl, Node, Python snippets and a one-click copy button.
- Create a sample repo: "redwood-sdk-playground-10min" with GitHub actions that runs the quick smoke test against a demo key. (linked artifact: github:repo/redwood-sdk-playground-10min)
- Add an interactive CLI command: redwood quickstart that verifies key, runs a lightweight generation, and prints a short troubleshooting hint if it fails.

Open questions / TODOs
- Should the quickstart default to streaming or sync? Tentatively sync for first run. (TODO: brief A/B test in user interviews)
- Ephemeral demo keys for internal pairing: maintain a small pool of short-lived keys scoped to pairing sessions, rotated daily. (Priya to own)
- Can we surface a one-line proxy for Next.js that people can paste into getServerSideProps? Draft snippet needed. (Marcos to draft)

Notes for engineering follow-up
- SDK: improve error messages to include remediation steps (PR: github:repo/redwood-sdk#456)
- Console: small UX tweak to show example copy-paste snippets for curl/Node/Python right next to newly created key
- Docs: add a troubleshooting section mapping HTTP codes to quick fixes (link: confluence:DX-SDK-Home#troubleshooting)

Appendix: Minimal serverless proxy (Vercel / Netlify friendly)
// api/proxy.js (Node, minimal)
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
export default async function handler(req, res){
  // NOTE: store REDWOOD_API_KEY as env var in the deployment (do not commit)
  const c = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  try{
    const out = await c.generate({ model: 'redwood-1-small', input: req.body.input || 'hello' });
    res.status(200).json({ text: out.text });
  } catch(e){
    console.error('proxy error', e);
    res.status(502).json({ error: 'upstream error; check logs' });
  }
}

Quick session script for Solutions Eng (clipboard copy)
1) echo -n $REDWOOD_API_KEY | pbcopy  # copy demo key on mac
2) curl example (paste) -> check output; if OK, proceed to Node demo
3) Open terminal, run: node index.js from Node example -> should print result

Final note
This is intentionally terse and prescriptive. The goal is to remove ambiguity during an onboarding call and reduce the number of times the SE pauses to check subtle environment issues. Keep this doc small; link out to extended tutorials after the initial success path is complete.

Versioning and history
- 2025-11-05: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-11-18: added Node/Python examples and appendix proxy (Liam)
- 2026-02-20: refreshed examples, added telemetry & quick session script (Marcos)

Unresolved items to capture in follow-up tickets
- DX-124: ephemeral demo key pool implementation and rotation flow
- DX-125: quickstart CLI design spec
- DX-126: add copy buttons and 1-line snippets in Console

Contact
For pairing or if you hit infra/keys issues, ping #dx-onboarding on Slack or DM Aisha.
